original_question: Let G be a finite simple transitive permutation group, and let δ(G) be the proportion of derangements in G. Is it true that δ(G) ⩾ 89/325? Note that δ(G) = 89/325 for the action of the Tits group G = 2 F4(2)′ on the cosets of a maximal parabolic subgroup of the form 22.[28 ].S3(Forum Math. Sigma, 13(2025), paper no. e98, 62 pp.).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.28 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of arXiv:1401.0300.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official problem almost verbatim: it has the correct class of groups (finite simple transitive permutation groups), the correct statistic δ(G), the exact proposed lower bound 89/325, and the sharpness example involving the Tits group ^2F_4(2)' acting on cosets of a maximal parabolic subgroup.
missing_details: The permutation domain should be named explicitly: one should say that G ≤ Sym(Ω) acts transitively on a finite set Ω.
For stand-alone readability, one should define a derangement as an element of G with no fixed points on Ω; this definition is supplied immediately before, in Problem 21.27.
δ(G) should be defined explicitly as the action-dependent proportion δ(G) = |{g ∈ G : g fixes no point of Ω}| / |G|.
If the sharpness note is retained, the action should be stated explicitly as the action of ^2F_4(2)' on the cosets of a maximal parabolic subgroup of shape 2^2.[2^8].S_3.
refined_question: Let G ≤ Sym(Ω) be a finite simple group acting transitively on a finite set Ω, and let δ(G) denote the proportion of derangements in this action, that is, δ(G) = |{g ∈ G : g fixes no point of Ω}| / |G|. Must one always have δ(G) ≥ 89/325? This bound would be best possible, since δ(G) = 89/325 when G = ^2F_4(2)' acts on the cosets of a maximal parabolic subgroup of shape 2^2.[2^8].S_3.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's official open problem exactly: Problem 21.28 asks whether every finite simple transitive permutation group has derangement proportion at least 89/325. The only nearby contextual definition needed to make the question fully stand-alone is the definition of a derangement, which appears immediately above in Problem 21.27. Because arXiv:1401.0300 is the Kourovka Notebook, not a standard article organized around Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3, those labels are not relevant here; the correct paper-faithful target is the numbered open problem 21.28 itself.
